mainEntity.name: How long does it take to construct an accessory dwelling unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building an ADU involves several distinct phases: design consultation, site planning, permitting, foundation and framing, MEP (mechanical, electrical, and plumbing) rough-ins, drywall, and finish installation. The overall schedule varies based on whether the unit is an attached addition, a garage conversion, or ground-up new construction. Project complexity changes significantly if trenching underground utility lines across the yard is required, or if the main electrical panel must be upgraded to support a secondary kitchen and water heater. Weather, permitting review times, and material lead times also influence completion schedules.
acceptedAnswer.description: Project timelines depend on whether it is a conversion or new build, with duration influenced by site planning, permitting, utility rough-ins, drywall installation, and finishes.
